title: A locally Cauchy sequence of sets converges locally in measure to a measurable set
statement: Let N ∈ ℕ and let (F_k)_{k∈ℕ} be L^N-null-measurable subsets of ℝ^N. Suppose that for every R ∈ ℕ and every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there is k₀ such that L^N(B_R(0) ∩ (F_k Δ F_l)) ≤ ε for all k, l ≥ k₀. Then there is a measurable G ⊆ ℝ^N such that L^N(K ∩ (F_k Δ G)) → 0 as k → ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^N.
lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (F : ℕ → Set (Rn N)), (∀ k, NullMeasurableSet (F k) volume) → (∀ (R : ℕ) (ε : ℝ≥0∞), 0 < ε → ∃ k₀ : ℕ, ∀ k ≥ k₀, ∀ l ≥ k₀, volume (Metric.ball (0 : Rn N) R ∩ symmDiff (F k) (F l)) ≤ ε) → ∃ G : Set (Rn N), MeasurableSet G ∧ ∀ K : Set (Rn N), IsCompact K → Tendsto (fun k ↦ volume (K ∩ symmDiff (F k) G)) atTop (𝓝 0)
